prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate objective function for a GNN-based netlist tier-partitioner (2-tier 3D IC).
Hypothesis of the change: Removing the soft criticality gate (crit^2) that over-suppresses non-critical neighbours and instead keeping the validated 0.7 locality coefficient unchanged is risky; the conservative refinement is to tighten the locality gate to crit^1.5 with the same 0.7 coefficient, which preserves the validated balance of critical-pair cohesion while letting moderately critical adjacent pairs also share a tier, reducing repair flips.
Rule-based digest (scores are improvement ratios vs. the official baseline; C1..C3 are the training circuits by size):
total=+0.124 robust(mean-std)=+0.005 min_case=+0.014 seed_std=0.045 tns_mean=+0.038 all_valid=True
  C1: score=+0.093 dWNS=+12.5% dTNS=+8.0% per-seed=[+0.06 +0.04 +0.18]
  C2: score=+0.014 dWNS=+1.2% dTNS=+2.8% per-seed=[+0.07 +0.01 -0.04]
  C3: score=+0.017 dWNS=+3.9% dTNS=+1.2% per-seed=[-0.01 +0.04 +0.02]
  partition stats vs baseline:
  C1: cut 137->146, wcut 421->430, crit_cross 0.011->0.016, repair_flips 103->119, changed-vs-baseline 17.2%
  C2: cut 318->304, wcut 1007->954, crit_cross 0.000->0.000, repair_flips 238->240, changed-vs-baseline 6.8%
  C3: cut 582->584, wcut 1955->1961, crit_cross 0.069->0.068, repair_flips 353->347, changed-vs-baseline 3.3%
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID, first classify the failure (crash / non-finite loss / balance repair failure / timeout) and whether it is systematic or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which circuit/metric moved and the plausible mechanism (cut nets, critical-pair cross-tier, repair flips)? (3) is the seed spread acceptable? (4) one concrete next step. No preamble.

response:
(1) Partially. Overall positive (total +0.124, robust +0.005) but the mechanism is not clean: C1 worsened on every partition metric (cut 137→146, crit_cross 0.011→0.016, repair_flips 103→119) despite the best score, so the crit^1.5 gate did not reduce flips where it mattered most.

(2) C2 drove the gain via fewer cut nets (318→304, wcut 1007→954) with flat crit_cross and flips; C3 marginal (flips 353→347). C1's regression suggests loosening the gate admitted moderately critical pairs that increased crossing and repair.

(3) Seed spread borderline: seed_std 0.045, C2 has a negative seed (-0.04); min_case +0.014 is thin.

(4) Next: sweep crit exponent 1.5→1.75 and locality coefficient jointly on C1 only, targeting repair_flips ≤ baseline before re-running full set.
